recommendation.recommendation: Implement immediate flood irrigation, supplement with additional water to offset rainfall deficit, and apply organic compost to raise soil organic carbon.
recommendation.justification: Satellite imagery shows critical vegetation stress (NDVI 0.154, NDWI -0.204) caused by high temperatures (31 °C) and below‑optimal rainfall. Soil chemistry is strong (pH 6.21, high nitrogen, suitable clay‑loam texture), but organic carbon is low, increasing moisture loss. Market prices are stable, so mitigating water stress now will preserve yield and profitability.
actions: Increase flood irrigation immediately to bring soil moisture to field capacity; water every 5‑7 days at 25‑30 mm per application.
Supplement the irrigation schedule today to compensate for the current rainfall deficit, maintaining soil moisture above wilting point for the next 2‑3 weeks.
Apply 5‑7 tons ha⁻¹ of well‑decomposed compost or organic manure within the next 7 days to raise organic carbon and improve water retention.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Reduced heat and water stress, improvement in NDVI to ≥0.4 within two weeks, stabilization of plant growth, and preservation of expected cotton yield and market revenue.
monitoring_plan: Daily visual inspection for wilting, leaf yellowing, and pest signs.
Measure soil moisture depth‑wise with tensiometers after each irrigation event.
Weekly NDVI/NDWI assessment via drone or satellite (cloud‑free) to track vegetation recovery.
Record temperature and humidity; adjust irrigation if daily max exceeds 30 °C for more than 3 consecutive days.
Re‑test soil organic carbon after 4 weeks to confirm improvement.
